summary: Restricted cron scheduling on node1 to root and opsadmin only by creating the opsadmin user and populating /etc/cron.allow, verified enforcement (denied for an unauthorized user, allowed for root/opsadmin), then restarted node1 and confirmed the boot identity changed and cron access control plus crond service survived the restart.
actions_performed: Inspected baseline cron config on node1 (no /etc/cron.allow present, opsadmin user did not exist)
Created /etc/cron.allow containing only root and opsadmin (root:root, 644)
Verified enforcement: unauthorized testuser denied crontab access, opsadmin and root allowed
Cleaned up test crontab entries and removed the temporary testuser
Captured pre-restart boot_id and cron.allow/crond state as baseline
Restarted node1 via systemctl reboot (backgrounded so the ack returned before disconnect)
Polled node1 until exec connectivity returned
Confirmed boot_id changed (bf4e9cbb... -> b260e20b...), proving an actual restart occurred

Verified post-restart recovery: crond active and enabled, /etc/cron.allow intact with root+opsadmin, opsadmin able to schedule a cron job successfully; removed the verification crontab entry afterward

evidence.requirement: Baseline: opsadmin user and cron config state before change
evidence.summary: Showed no /etc/cron.allow existed and opsadmin user did not exist prior to remediation
useradd -m opsadmin succeeded, id shows uid=1000(opsadmin)

evidence.requirement: /etc/cron.allow restricts cron to root and opsadmin
evidence.summary: Created /etc/cron.allow containing exactly root and opsadmin

evidence.requirement: Enforcement verified: only root/opsadmin can schedule cron jobs
evidence.summary: testuser denied crontab access (exit 1, 'not allowed to use this program'); opsadmin and root both succeeded (exit 0)
Removed test crontab entries and deleted the temporary testuser after killing its lingering session

evidence.requirement: Pre-restart baseline (boot identity, crond health, cron.allow)
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id bf4e9cbb-84f9-45f0-9b81-6602b98cea07, crond active, cron.allow=root/opsadmin before reboot
Backgrounded systemctl reboot command acknowledged (reboot_scheduled) before the connection dropped

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart proof via changed boot identity
evidence.summary: Connection timed out/reset during reboot, then reconnected with new boot_id b260e20b-a184-48e7-8ce5-f2636b6cde50, proving an actual restart

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of cron access control and service
evidence.summary: crond active/enabled, /etc/cron.allow intact with root+opsadmin, and opsadmin successfully scheduled and the entry was then removed, confirming durable enforcement after restart
